titleEn: A seed is a sound, a vowel and a hum. Ga + a + ṃ = gaṃ — and gaṃ is Gaṇeśa.
meaningEn: Every seed syllable is built the same way: a sound, a vowel, and the hum written as a dot above (ṃ). The Gaṇapati Atharvaśīrṣa takes gaṃ apart in front of you — 'the letter ga is the first form, a the middle, the anusvāra the last; the dot is above, and the nāda joins them.' Most seeds close in that hum. A few close in a breath (ḥ — sauḥ, hrīḥ) or a stop (phaṭ). Once the shape is seen, every seed on this shelf reads the same way.
meaningHi: हर बीज-अक्षर एक ही तरह बनता है: एक आवाज़, एक स्वर, और ऊपर की बिंदी वाली गूँज (ं)। गणपति अथर्वशीर्ष गं को सामने खोलकर दिखाता है — 'ग पहला रूप है, अ बीच का, अनुस्वार आख़िरी; ऊपर बिंदु है, और नाद इन्हें जोड़ता है।' ज़्यादातर बीज इसी गूँज पर ख़त्म होते हैं। कुछ साँस पर (ः — सौः, ह्रीः) या झटके पर (फट्)। एक बार यह ढाँचा दिख गया, तो इस शेल्फ़ का हर बीज ऐसे ही पढ़ा जाता है।
sayItLike: ga · a · mmm → gum (short, like 'gun' ending in a hum)

words.glossEn: the consonant — the body of the seed
the vowel — the breath that lets it sound
words.glossHi: स्वर — वह साँस जिससे आवाज़ निकलती है

words.glossEn: the dot (ं) — anusvāra, the hum that closes it
words.glossHi: बिंदी (ं) — अनुस्वार, गूँज जो इसे बंद करती है
words.grammar: 'the anusvāra is the last form'; written as the dot above the letter

words.glossEn: the dot — the hum drawn to a point
words.glossHi: बिंदु — गूँज एक बिंदी में सिमटी
words.grammar: 'bindu is the upper form' — the written dot and the sound narrowing to nothing

words.glossEn: the fading tone — what joins the parts into one
words.glossHi: नाद — वह धीमी होती आवाज़ जो सबको एक कर देती है
words.grammar: 'nāda is the joining'; the tail of the hum after the lips close

source.text: Gaṇapati Atharvaśīrṣa §8; Śāradā-tilaka Tantra (Lakṣmaṇa Deśika, 11th c.), chapters 1–2 on the letters (mātṛkā)
source.ref: Atharvaśīrṣa §8: gakāraḥ pūrvarūpam · akāro madhyamarūpam · anusvāraś cāntyarūpam · bindur uttararūpam · nādaḥ sandhānam
source.note: The Atharvaśīrṣa is a late Upaniṣad (c. 16th–17th c.) — 'Upaniṣad' in a title does not mean Vedic-era. 'Most seeds close in a hum' is deliberate: sauḥ and hrīḥ close in a breath, phaṭ in a stop.

significance.textSays: Atharvaśīrṣa §8: the seed gaṃ is ga + a + anusvāra, with bindu above and nāda joining — 'this is the Gaṇeśa-vidyā.' Scripture doing its own dissection.
significance.traditionSays: The Tantras treat the fifty letters as the Devī's own body (mātṛkā) and build every seed from them; a seed is meant to be heard as one fused sound, the parts felt but not separated.
significance.weDoNotClaim: That the sound has a power of its own, or a dictionary meaning. This card shows how a seed is spelled and how it is voiced — nothing more.

practice.timeOfDay: any time — a listening lesson, not a japa
